# Performance

In the context of the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (AKDB) in [[danmark|Denmark]], "Performance" refers to the systematic tracking of clinical and operational quality metrics for acute surgical patients. The database evaluates hospitals and regions across a series of standardized indicators (Indikator 1 through 11) that measure the timeliness of initial assessments, surgical interventions, post-operative care protocols, and patient survival rates. The data reveals a healthcare system that generally meets national mortality targets but struggles significantly with the timeliness of acute interventions and post-operative mobilization.

## Timeliness of Initial Care
A major theme in the performance data is the systemic shortfall in timely initial interventions. For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], which tracks the administration of antibiotics within three hours of arrival, national performance was only 30.5% in the 2022–2023 period [^src1] and 34.4% in 2023–2024 [^src12]. These results fall far short of the development goals of >60% or 90% [^src3] [^src7]. The median time from hospital arrival to antibiotic administration was 4.4 to 5 hours nationally [^src6] [^src8]. Similarly, [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] (CT scans within two hours) hovered around 30% to 32% compliance [^src3] [^src7], and [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] failed to meet its ≥90% standard at either the national or regional level [^src8].

## Surgical and Post-Operative Care
Performance in surgical timeliness and post-operative protocols also shows widespread room for improvement. [[indikator-4x|Indikator 4x]] and [[indikator-4y|Indikator 4y]], which relate to surgery within 6 or 24 hours for specific conditions, missed the ≥90% development goals [^src4]. For [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] (mobilization within 24 hours), national performance was 35.6%, and not a single reporting unit met the ≥90% target [^src5] [^src7]. Nutrition assessment within 48 hours ([[indikator-7|Indikator 7]]) was achieved for only 26.2% of patients [^src7] [^src17], while epidural anesthesia ([[indikator-8|Indikator 8]]) was utilized in 52.2% of eligible cases [^src7]. 

## Mortality and Survival
Despite the documented delays in acute interventions, mortality outcomes generally meet national targets. [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] (30-day mortality) met the <18% (or <15%) goal nationally, recording a result of 11% overall [^src11] and 6.4% in a specific analyzed cohort [^src9]. [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] (90-day mortality) also met its <20% target with a 15% result [^src11]. However, 30-day mortality for patients with a [[charlson-score-1-2|Charlson Score = 1 eller 2]] varied drastically among individual hospitals. For example, mortality ranged from 0.0% at [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] to 25.0% at [[holbaek-sygehus|Holbæk Sygehus]] and 100.0% at [[nykoebing-f-sygehus|Nykøbing F Sygehus]], though the latter figures are heavily influenced by very small sample sizes [^src9].

## Regional and Hospital Variations
The data highlights distinct regional disparities in performance compliance. For Indikator 1, [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland — Midtjylland]] consistently led the country with compliance rates around 39.8% to 44.6% [^src1] [^src12]. In contrast, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark — Syddanmark]] lagged significantly, recording rates between 13.5% and 22.5% [^src1] [^src12]. Meanwhile, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden — Hovedstaden]] demonstrated administrative improvements, increasing its data reporting frequency from approximately 65% to 75% over a two-year period [^src2].
